formula: ±"Your medical source"*−"qualified medical source as defined in § 416.919g"
rendered: Your medical source is not a qualified medical source as defined in § 416.919g
caveats: Treats the context-fixed singular phrase 'Your medical source' as one fixed reference. The engine does not resolve 'your'; this is the project's engineering convention for singular descriptions.
rationale: With the addressee and source fixed by the surrounding provision, this is one negative predication. The section reference qualifies the predicate term; it does not import the referenced rule.
nl: Your medical source is not a qualified medical source as defined in § 416.919g.

formula: ±ADA*+"Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)"*
rendered: ADA is Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
rationale: Both sides name one Act. Wild quantity over two singular terms is the engine's identity form, so the formula gives a symmetric naming identity rather than a one-way class inclusion.
nl: ADA means the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.).

formula: −Selection+("is subject to"±"income-eligibility and income-targeting requirements in § 5.653"*)
rendered: every selection is subject to income-eligibility and income-targeting requirements in § 5.653
caveats: Treats the coordinated requirements in § 5.653 as the one named requirement bundle used by the source sentence; it does not formalize the contents of § 5.653.
rationale: The generic subject receives universal force and the verb phrase is a binary relation to the uniquely named requirement bundle. 'However' marks discourse contrast and adds no truth-conditional clause.
nl: However, selection is subject to the income-eligibility and income-targeting requirements in § 5.653.

rendered: every federally administered state supplementary payment is ssi benefit
rationale: In 'SSI benefits include any X', the asserted direction is every X is an SSI benefit. 'Also' presupposes other members of the benefit class but does not add a second asserted restriction.
nl: SSI benefits also include any federally administered State supplementary payments.

rationale: Regulatory 'means' gives an exhaustive class definition: every nonmedical source has the stated properties and every source with those properties is a nonmedical source. The noted A-form states only the first direction. General-term coextension needs two TFL propositions, which the one-proposition policy forbids.
nl: Nonmedical source means a source of evidence who is not a medical source.

formula: ±"Disability program"*+"Federal program for providing supplemental security income benefits for the blind and disabled under title XVI of the Act, as amended"*
rendered: Disability program is Federal program for providing supplemental security income benefits for the blind and disabled under title XVI of the Act, as amended
caveats: Treats both noun phrases as singular names of one program. The term-logic literature reviewed by this project supplies no dedicated definite-description theory, so this remains an engineering convention.
rationale: Unlike a general class definition, the source identifies a defined singular label with the one Federal program named by the full description. Singular identity is expressible in one proposition without reducing 'means' to one-way inclusion.
nl: Disability program means the Federal program for providing supplemental security income benefits for the blind and disabled under title XVI of the Act, as amended.

formula: ±ADA*+"Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)"*
rendered: ADA is Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
rationale: Exact duplicate of r41, deliberately retained because the sampling protocols preserve repetition. It receives the same singular-identity formula and judgment.
nl: ADA means the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.).

formula: ±"Section 214"*+"section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980, as amended (42 U.S.C. 1436a)"*
rendered: Section 214 is section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980, as amended (42 U.S.C. 1436a)
rationale: Both sides are singular legal names for one statutory section. The Act name, amendment qualifier, and citation all remain inside the second name; no referenced rule is incorporated.
nl: Section 214 means section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980, as amended (42 U.S.C. 1436a).
